entries.text: should answered sit on the ask line?
detail: On the ask line's dividing rule, at its right end. Decisions then sat on the open questions' rule the same way, so one pattern held across the page: a heading rule names what is behind a key and shows its state.

entries.text: can a thing have two kinds?
detail: No. When something seems to need two kinds, it is two linked things.

B3 Group Design Project is a course on Canvas, and 3YP is the repo where you do its work: two items with a link between them, which is why 3YP felt like it belonged in three places. One kind each, joined by links, keeps the backend's rules simple.

entries.text: Round 2d: each capability where its context is; studies on Home; ADR-006 revised
detail: Project view: dossier centred in the top border, decisions beside the open questions (new, from the dossier), the timeline in New's heading, answered at the end of the ask line; left and right walk the branches from anywhere, starting at the newest; nabla's full branch history.
Home: careers | studies, studies holding courses and coursework with what is due, learning opening from its last row; projects is the Projects area.
ADR-006: areas say where, kinds say what, one global taxonomy, with the full grid. ProjectKind repo | course | application; ProjectView.questions, .due.

entries.text: are tutorial sheets their own type, or coursework?
detail: Their own type, sheet, alongside coursework. Both are tasks linked to a course, and both can carry a deadline, which any task can have.
Sheets are separate because they are planned differently: about five hours in two or three blocks, every week, where coursework needs its own estimate. Merging them would lose that.

entries.text: what is the difference between goals and threads?
detail: They are unrelated. A goal is a purpose for learning, such as Jump internship preparation. A mail thread is an email conversation.
An earlier table said "thread (keryx)", and that bracket was the confusion: it named the app that stores mail, which plays no part in labelling.

entries.text: is the taxonomy global?
detail: Yes. Every item, in every project and every app, carries two independent labels: its area (where it belongs in your life) and its kind (what shape of thing it is).
Both are defined once in the shared root and read by everything. The brackets naming kairos or keryx only said which app stores a thing, so they are gone.

entries.text: locus session: a recreated view goes back to its place

entries.text: Round 1, Home: sections by kind of work, Tab and arrows move, a sender not a doer
detail: Home gets three kinds of work under their own headings: projects (what you build), careers (applications and the CV), learning (goals). kairos and keryx become parts of locus. Approve shrinks to one 'waiting for you' line; Explore is grouped by kind, titles only, no grading here. Counts say what they count; sessions carry a plain summary (Session.summary). The moment sits centred in the frame; running jobs pulse; the budget names both limits. The work grid fills the width.

Tab cycles sections everywhere; arrows walk a section and run into the next. The selected row is a full-width band. Enter on a project hands it to the Project window (a peek file and tmux select-window); Esc there returns home and following resumes. test-follow.sh checks the handoff.
The round's notes, and his seeds for later pages, are in slice-1.md Rounds.

entries.text: deliver: an existing folder is not reported created; skill: -{}- for a literal --
detail: rmapi v0.0.35 prints "entry already exists" and exits 0, so `_ensure_folder` reported "(created folder)" on every push to /Inbox. The message is checked before the exit code. Found by the Slice 0.4 check, as was `\texttt{--all-extras}` printing as `-all-extras`, now in the skill.

entries.text: Slice 0.4: the one-column test ignores the page number; cli comment
Slice 0.4: LaTeX to the tablet in one column with even margins
detail: The device preamble drops `twocolumn`: one column at 10pt inside 0.95in margins on all four sides, the geometry of the redesign plan documents (7.07 x 9.43in), with their 1.08 leading. The margin is a new LaTeX-only setting, [reading].latex_margin_in, so the markdown path and the daily page keep margin_in; latex_font_pt defaults to 10. The title is a plain heading now that nothing needs to span two columns. The MCP tool docstring, the `remarkable` command, the remarkable-explainer skill and CLAUDE.md say the same.

tex2pdf decoded the compiler's output strictly, so a non-UTF-8 byte in a log raised UnicodeDecodeError inside subprocess.run and the send died with a decode error instead of the compile's result. Decoded with errors="replace"; a fake engine plants the byte on both streams in the test, for a passing and a failing compile.

entries.text: Slice 1 step 1.4: first pass of every screen
detail: All 16 screens draw from the fixtures at 95x38: Home (next, mail, the rhythm grid, projects with their sessions, explore beside approve, system), the Project view with its branch graph (plan D.1: a lane per branch, collapsed to fork, length and merge), Decisions, Answered and Changes, System and Budget, Explore (queue cards with their reasoning, strike reasons), Approve, the automatic-actions log, Ink confirm with the crop through ratatui-image (kitty in Ghostty; half blocks in --dump), Search, the 8-week area chart, Interview prep, Learning (goals, syllabus, tracks, sheets) and the weekly review's five steps.

Actions do their visual part and the footer says what they would have done; nothing leaves the process. Each screen module carries its own keys, tried before the global ones, and lists them in the ? overlay.

The image protocol is asked for only when Ink confirm first opens, with a 500 ms ceiling: asked at startup, a terminal that never answers cost 2 s before the first frame (measured on a tmux server with nothing behind it).

Fixtures: G-Research open with no plan, Millennium finished; the ink crop is synthetic (tools/make_ink_crop.py). --dump --project opens a project with no tmux session; --timing prints load and per-screen draw times.

Tests: every screen on both sets, every active project's screens, each review step and Explore tab, the keys overlay everywhere, and every key pressed on every screen, all within the window; snapshots of all 16.

entries.text: status: uncovered alias surfaces are no longer a warning
detail: Slice 0.3 took `locus link` out of the nightly unit, so the count only grows and the warning "rerun `locus link`" would print every day with nothing to clear it. The count stays on the alias substrate line.

entries.text: Slice 1 step 1.3: contracts for every screen, the default and empty fixture sets
detail: locus-contract gains a first cut of what each of the 16 screens shows: the taxonomy and registry (every kind of work is a project: code, light, course, opportunity), the Project view with its branch graph, Decisions, Answered, Changes, Home's own lines and the work section, System and usage, Explore, approve, the auto log, ink confirm, search, the learning system with interview prep, and the weekly review. Every struct refuses unknown fields.

The default set is a Saturday evening across the real projects: branch graphs, decision titles and the Jump Trading prep (format, topics, the seven daily sheets, scores from error log v6) are real; the rest is by hand (fixtures/README.md says which). The empty set is generated from it.

locus-tui --validate-fixtures loads both sets strictly and cross-checks them (project ids, tracks, ink fixtures, usage totals, unread files); tests break the default set on purpose to show each check fires.

entries.text: Slice 0.3: nothing old runs at night
detail: Off: locus-daily, locus-daily-pull, locus-discover-harvest (removed from deploy/systemd/enabled). locus-maintain now runs only `structure --unstructured --limit 20` and records completion; link, recall enrolment and questions, intent --act, answer-marks, connections, tensions and the discover reading steps are gone from it. health drops the three switched-off kinds from its expected cadence, or `locus status` would call them overdue within three days. The code stays until its removal commit later in the slice.

entries.text: locus session: views come back after a restart
detail: tmux-resurrect restores the view windows by name as bare shells. Windows the session script starts carry @locus-view, which resurrect does not restore, so ensure respawns any view window without it; a client landing on locus runs ensure. ensure is serialised with a tmux wait-for lock, since the landing hook and an Alt key otherwise race to create the same window. test-follow.sh checks a mock restore.

entries.text: what is the failed glyph?
detail: The Nerd Font symbol that marks a failed job or session, such as a tablet push that hit the rate limit. It should pair with kairos's done box.

kairos's done box is the outline style (md-checkbox_marked_outline), so the matching failed glyph is md-close_box_outline, the one the plan named. An earlier note had suggested the filled box by mistake.

entries.text: locus-session.sh: a view that fails keeps its window open on the error
detail: keryx with no config exits at once, and its window vanished without a word.

entries.text: laptop outbox: the repo copy keeps the area folders (matches the installed script)
Rename the data directory vault/ -> data/ (ADR-005, migration 0037)
detail: `vault/` read as an Obsidian vault (and held one). Paths under it are identity keys: an edited note is found again by its source_uri, so a directory rename alone would have filed every edited note as a second document. Migration 0037 rewrites the stored paths in the 14 key/location columns (1,549 rows on the server, trialled on a copy), only where `vault/` is followed by one of the directory's own entries, so `locus/vault/` code paths and corpus text are untouched.

server-sync.sh moves the server's directory once, under the ingest flock, and rewrites its config.toml (copy kept as config.toml.bak-pre-data). Placeholders are untracked except data/.gitkeep, so the pull cannot collide with the move. User-facing wording says "library"; model prompts are unchanged so pass caches stay valid.

entries.text: Drop folder holds sources: personal/ is its own category; area drops are never his writing
detail: ADR-003 follow-up. `personal/` mapped to `note`, which with a text format counted as owner- authored, so a third-party .docx dropped there would have had beliefs drawn from it as his. `personal/` now files as `personal`, and `is_area_drop` excludes every area folder from the owner-authored rule in both its Python and SQL forms. The old `projects/` folder shares the area's name, so its two OQTS specs flip to sources (accepted).

Tests pin [structure].belief_source_* to the code defaults: config.example.toml still said ["note"], so a laptop config copied from it failed the owner-authored tests. The example now matches the defaults.

entries.text: Slice 1 step 1.2: the locus tmux session, Alt-1..4, Project view follows
detail: crates/locus-tui/tmux/: locus.tmux (Alt-1..4 only on the locus session, else passed through; client-session-changed/client-attached hooks in slot 42), locus-session.sh (idempotent: recreates a closed view), focus-hook.sh (atomic write of the project window's session, locus and aulos ignored). The Project view follows <state>/focus, holds while a key was pressed in the last 5 s or a detail screen is open, and m pins it. test-follow.sh checks all of it on a private tmux server (-L locus-test -f /dev/null).

entries.text: Fold the shared Rust crates into the repo (ADR-004)
detail: One workspace at the root: crates/{eco-dates,locus-theme,locus-contract, locus-tui}, replacing tui/. eco-dates copied verbatim from locus-shared main (d2191b2), locus-theme from its theme branch (b74d7a0). kairos and keryx keep their pins; each moves to this repo when next touched.

entries.text: Slice 1 step 1.1: tui workspace, app shell, use log, --dump
detail: locus-tui runs Home or Project with every screen of the spec's table as a placeholder: section focus by letter, Enter/Esc/?//, the footer, R to reset, a local use log with --use-report. --dump prints a screen as text; a test renders every screen on both fixture sets at 95x38 and checks display width. The theme is locus-theme in locus-shared (formerly eco).

entries.text: Slice 1 step 1.0: screens v2 reference into the repo
Slice 1: spec, decisions D1-D6 answered, approved
ADR-003 revised: the drop folder is organised by area
detail: The system cannot label arrivals yet, so a flat drop would be filed `uncategorized`. ~/LocusDrop/ now has studies/ projects/ careers/ personal/ (the notes-repository tree), and `_category` maps each onto the category the library still keys behaviour on (studies -> coursework, ...). The course or project folder below survives in source_uri for the labeller.
The watcher's repository drops are retired: `projects/<name>/` is an area folder of ordinary files now, and the plan removes repository ingest. Existing `locusdrop:` documents are untouched.

entries.text: ADR-003: one flat drop folder; the system labels what arrives
fix(tests): loop B tests wrote fake PDFs into the live vault/incoming
detail: Three direct annotate_sync calls left ingest_fn and promote_fn at their defaults, the real ingest and promote. A /Reading/Finished document counts as chosen, so every run of the file wrote "%PDF-1.4 fake paper bytes" into the live vault/incoming/paper/ as "A Paper.pdf" (there since 6 Aug, recreated by a server test run on 19 Oct). With locus-watch now consuming that folder, it would have been quarantined every time the suite ran.

entries.text: Slice 0.2: locus-watch, the drop zone's only consumer
detail: Nothing ran `locus watch` between 6 Sep and 19 Oct, so files dropped into vault/incoming/ sat there. Discovery accepts and hand-added books kept arriving because they ingest in place, which hid the dead drop zone. A 5-minute oneshot timer (`locus watch --once`), incoming only: repository ingest is retired by the plan, so `watch-repo` stays unscheduled.

entries.text: Slice 0.1: one deploy flow, laptop -> GitHub -> server
detail: deploy/deploy.sh pushes main, fast-forwards the server checkout (refused over uncommitted changes) and hands over to deploy/server-sync.sh from the code just pulled: uv sync --all-extras (a bare sync would uninstall torch and the other extras the server runs), backup + `locus migrate` when a migration arrived, unit files installed from deploy/systemd/, the enabled set made equal to deploy/systemd/enabled, and long-running services restarted when the code moved.

The server-only locus-remarkable-receiver.service is adopted into the repo unchanged. The manifest lists exactly what is enabled today, so this first deploy changes nothing that runs. `locus migrate` is new: it prints the schema revision before and after, so a deploy can say where it left the DB.

Redesign: plan v4 in the repo, CLAUDE.md section 0, decision log, Slice 0 spec

CLAUDE.md gains a section 0 that orients to the redesign and says which engine sections are being removed; the existing sections stay intact and shrink slice by slice. docs/decisions/ starts locus's own log (provisional format until Slice 2). slices/slice-0.md is the Slice 0 spec, awaiting approval.
